title: Geometrically maximal tori over finite fields
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and fix an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups below are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group which becomes $\mathbf G_m^r$ over $\bar k$, for some integer $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Unipotent means admitting, for some $n\geq1$, a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] into the upper unitriangular group $\mathcal U_{n,k}\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]: its $A$-points are upper triangular matrices with all diagonal entries $1$, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Assume $k$ is finite and let $G$ be smooth and connected. Its scalar extension $G_{\bar k}$ is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type over $\bar k$. There is a torus $T\subseteq G$ defined over $k$ such that $T_{\bar k}$ is maximal among torus subgroups of $G_{\bar k}$: every torus subgroup $S\subseteq G_{\bar k}$ containing $T_{\bar k}$ is equal to $T_{\bar k}$. The rank-zero torus is allowed. There is no reductivity assumption on $G$.

source.place: Proposition 17.99, printed pp.383–384, in the finite-field setting of section 17.k: existence of a Borel pair with geometrically maximal torus. This is exactly its use in the final paragraph of Proposition 17.81, p.379. Geometric connectedness uses Proposition 1.34, pp.16–17; smoothness is stable under field extension.

proof.text: Put $F=\bar k$ and $H=G_F$. The field-extension clause of [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products] says that smooth connected group schemes remain smooth and connected under every field extension, so it applies to $G$ without any solvability hypothesis. Affineness of $H$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Writing $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$ with $C$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra, its base change is $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_k F)$; the same finite list of algebra generators generates over $F$. Thus $H$ also has finite type. This proves the scalar-extension clause of the item.

source.place: Proposition 1.34, pp.16–17; base-change preparation for Proposition 17.99, pp.383–384.

proof.text: The rank-zero torus $1\subseteq H$ is a torus. By the torus-containment clause of [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety], choose a Borel subgroup $B\subseteq H$ containing it. By [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy], $B$ contains a torus $T_0$ maximal in $H$. Let $\sigma$ act semilinearly through $a\mapsto a^q$ on $F$, as in [def-weil-frobenius-substitution], where $q=|k|$. Applying this field automorphism and its inverse to closed subgroup inclusions and split-torus isomorphisms shows that $\sigma(T_0)$ is again a maximal torus. The conjugacy clause of [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy] gives $h\in G(F)$ such that $\sigma(T_0)=hT_0h^{-1}$ as subgroup schemes.

source.place: Proposition 17.99, first proof paragraph, printed p.384; direct maximal-torus conjugacy version of its Frobenius argument, using Theorem 17.10.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-lang-finite-field-group-surjectivity] to the given smooth connected affine finite-type group $G/k$ and to $h^{-1}$. Choose $g\in G(F)$ with $g^{-1}\sigma(g)=h^{-1}$, equivalently $\sigma(g)h=g$. Set $T_1=gT_0g^{-1}$. Conjugation is a group-scheme automorphism, so $T_1$ is a maximal torus of $H$. Moreover, as equalities of closed subgroup schemes, $$\sigma(T_1)=\sigma(g)\sigma(T_0)\sigma(g)^{-1}=\sigma(g)hT_0h^{-1}\sigma(g)^{-1}=gT_0g^{-1}=T_1.$$ This calculation is scheme-theoretic because the preceding conjugacy was an equality of subgroup schemes and conjugation commutes with scalar extension.

source.place: Proposition 17.99, first proof paragraph, printed p.384; direct maximal-torus conjugacy version of its Frobenius argument, using Theorem 17.10.

proof.text: We make the descent finite rather than assume an infinite-extension version of a finite descent theorem. Write $T_1=\operatorname{Spec}((C\otimes_k F)/I)$. The algebra $C\otimes_k F$ is Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], so choose finitely many generators $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ of $I$, using [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Each $f_i$ is a finite sum of tensors. Adjoin their finitely many coefficients to $k$ inside $F$, obtaining a finite field extension $E/k$; it is finite since each coefficient is algebraic and $k$ is finite. Put $C_E=C\otimes_k E$, $I_E=(f_1,\ldots,f_s)\subseteq C_E$, and $Z_E=\operatorname{Spec}(C_E/I_E)$. Its extension to $F$ is exactly $T_1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], $I_E$ is the contraction of $I$ to $C_E$.

source.place: Appendix A.65, printed p.581; explicit finite-coefficient reduction of the descent used in Proposition 17.99.

proof.text: The closed subscheme $Z_E$ is a subgroup, not merely a model of its underlying scheme. Use the coordinate multiplication, counit and antipode of [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. For each generator $f_i$, its counit vanishes after extension to $F$, its antipode lies in $I$ after extension, and its comultiplication lies in $I\otimes_F C_F+C_F\otimes_F I$, because $T_1$ is a subgroup. Apply faithful flatness and ideal contraction from [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat, lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] to $E\to F$, $C_E\to C_F$, and $(C_E\otimes_E C_E)\to(C_F\otimes_F C_F)$. These three assertions hold already over $E$, with the comultiplication ideal $I_E\otimes_E C_E+C_E\otimes_E I_E$. The resulting maps on $C_E/I_E$ give the restricted group law, identity and inverse; their identities follow from those on $G_E$. Hence $Z_E\subseteq G_E$ is a closed subgroup scheme.

source.place: Appendix A.64–A.65, printed pp.580–581; coordinate explanation of subgroup descent.

proof.text: The finite field $E$ is preserved by $\sigma$. From $\sigma(I)=I$ and the contraction identity $I_E=I\cap C_E$ we get $\sigma(I_E)=I_E$, so $Z_E$ is preserved as a closed subgroup by this semilinear automorphism. By [lem-sfb-finite-field-galois-frobenius], $E/k$ is finite Galois and every automorphism is a power of $a\mapsto a^q$. Thus $Z_E$ is preserved by the entire Galois group. Apply [lem-sfb-galois-closed-subscheme-descent] with $X=G$ to obtain a closed $k$-subgroup $T\subseteq G$ whose $E$-extension is $Z_E$. Its $F$-extension is $T_1$, so it is a torus by the definition in the item. Finally if a torus $S\subseteq G_F$ contains $T_F=T_1=gT_0g^{-1}$, then $g^{-1}Sg$ contains $T_0$, whence $g^{-1}Sg=T_0$ by maximality; therefore $S=T_F$. All arguments allow rank zero and use no reductivity.

source.place: Proposition 17.99, first proof paragraph, p.384; Appendix A.65, p.581; finite-field Frobenius as in section 17.k, p.382.
